name: Isoproterenol mesotherapy

lead: Isoproterenol (isoprenaline) is a synthetic catecholamine that activates beta-adrenergic receptors. Beta stimulation can trigger lipolysis, the release of stored fat from fat cells, so it was tried in injections around fatty areas in lipolytic mesotherapy.
The appearance goal is local slimming, such as thighs. The evidence is a small 1990s controlled trial of five women reported alongside topical-cream trials, so the research base is small.

paras: In mesotherapy a practitioner places small injections into the skin or fat of the target area, with trial subjects also following a diet and walking. The research describes injections at intervals around one thigh, with the other thigh as a control. This wiki does not give dosing or procedure details.

Isoproterenol is a prescription drug for heart rhythm and shock settings. Its listed adverse effects include fast heartbeat, palpitations, arrhythmias, angina and blood-pressure changes, and infusions have provoked panic attacks in controlled studies. Mesotherapy in general is regulated by medical boards, and infections have been reported with unregulated practice.

chain: Isoproterenol activates beta receptors on fat cells
Targeted area slims, with diet and walking in the trial
angle.text: Practitioners and the 1995 trial authors proposed that beta stimulation could slim a localised fat area such as the thigh. Trial participants also dieted and walked.

lead: Isoproterenol, also called isoprenaline, is a synthetic catecholamine and full agonist of beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors. It is used in medicine for slow heart rate, heart block and some shock states. [1][2]

In mesotherapy, a technique of intradermal or subcutaneous micro-injections, beta-agonists have been proposed to promote local fat loss, since beta-adrenergic stimulation can start lipolysis in fat cells. [3][4]

A 1995 controlled series reported in Obesity Research began with five overweight women who received isoproterenol injections around one thigh three times weekly for four weeks with diet and walking, while later trials moved to topical creams. [4]
infobox: Prescription; injectable only in US for medical use [1]

paras: Isoproterenol is the N-isopropyl analogue of norepinephrine and epinephrine and a full agonist at beta-1 and beta-2 receptors with little alpha activity at lower concentrations. [1] The theoretical basis for fat use is that beta stimulation, alpha-2 inhibition or phosphodiesterase inhibition can each start lipolysis, and thigh fat in women is described as harder to mobilise because of alpha-2 receptor activity. [4]

Mesotherapy involves injecting substances such as vitamins, enzymes, plant extracts and hyaluronic acid into skin or fat, and fat reduction is one of its claimed uses. A Wikipedia overview says cosmetic efficacy is unproven by standard trials, that US state medical boards regulate practitioners, that several South American countries ban it, and that France briefly banned it for fat removal in 2011 before lifting the ban. [5]

Listed effects of isoproterenol include tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias, angina, headache, tremor, sweating and blood-pressure changes. [1] In a placebo-controlled study, infusions provoked panic attacks in 66 percent of panic-disorder patients and 9 percent of controls. [6] Reports of mesotherapy harms include abscesses and a mycobacterial infection cluster in clients of an unregulated Australian salon. [5]
Isoproterenol was discovered in 1940 and introduced in the US in 1947 as an early synthetic sympathomimetic. [1]

The 1995 Obesity Research paper describes five controlled trials using one thigh as a double-blinded control. Trial 1 gave isoproterenol injections to five overweight women over four weeks with diet and walking; trials 2 to 5 used topical forskolin, yohimbine and aminophylline ointments in groups of 5 to 30 women. The excerpted abstract does not give outcome results for the injections. [4] No other trials of injected isoproterenol for fat reduction are listed in the sources.

timeline.event: Obesity Research reports controlled trials of topical fat reduction, including isoproterenol injections around one thigh. [4]
